description: The Fire Rat in Chinese astrology: personality, Fire element traits, 1936 and 1996 dates and compatibility.
answer: In Chinese astrology, the Fire Rat is the Rat born in a Fire year, one of five versions of the first animal. It combines the Rat's quick wits with Fire's qualities. Fire Rat years between 1924 and 2044 are 1936 and 1996. The Rat's fixed element is Water.

sections.heading: The Fire Rat personality
paragraphs: A Fire Rat brings heat and urgency to an animal usually known for careful calculation. Here the year stem and the Rat's built-in Water element sit on opposite sides of the controlling cycle, since Water controls Fire, and readings often describe a person who carries both a cool head and a hot temperament. Fire Rats are pictured as energetic, outspoken and adventurous, quicker to act on an idea than most Rats and more willing to take a public stand. Their charm is vivid and their opinions strong. The Water underneath tends to keep that fire from running completely wild, adding shrewd timing and a sense of when to pull back, but the inner tug between impulse and caution can leave them restless.

Fire is the element of summer and full daylight, and a Fire year is traditionally said to turn up the volume of whatever animal it meets. Descriptions link it with passion, charisma, courage and a love of movement and expression. Fire-year people are often portrayed as lively, persuasive and quick to act, able to warm a room and rally others behind an idea. The element is associated with the heart and with joy, which gives it real generosity of spirit. Its traditional shadow is impatience: Fire can burn hot and fast, leading to restlessness, sharp words in the moment and a tendency to lose interest once the excitement fades.

sections.heading: Fire Rat at work and in love
paragraphs: At work, Fire is usually linked with initiative, persuasion and visible leadership. Fire-year people are often described as the ones who launch things, pitch ideas and keep morale high when a deadline looms, which suits performance, sales, media, entrepreneurship and campaigning of every kind. They tend to thrive on momentum and recognition. The traditional caution concerns stamina and follow-through: a Fire stem may lose patience with routine detail, so pairing with methodical colleagues and pacing energy across a project usually helps.

Give a Fire Rat a negotiation and it often comes alive. This version of the sign pairs a calculating mind with a theatrical streak, so pitching, trading, campaign strategy, journalism and live events are frequently named as natural ground. Colleagues admire the speed and occasionally wince at the bluntness, which is why a cooling-off rule before sending a sharp email saves a great deal of goodwill. Romantically, the Fire Rat is attentive and flirtatious, keen to impress with clever gifts and last-minute plans. It wants someone who can trade banter without taking every quip to heart. The familiar flashpoint is jealousy laced with worry: when it senses a threat to security, sparks fly quickly and the apology arrives rather more slowly.

sections.heading: Fire Rat years and dates
paragraphs: Fire Rat years in the Lunar New Year table run from January 24, 1936 to February 10, 1937 and from February 19, 1996 to February 6, 1997. Because the year begins at Lunar New Year, a birthday in January or early February needs checking: in 1996 anyone born before Feb 19 is a Wood Pig, not a Fire Rat. Sixty years separate each Fire Rat year, the length of a full round of five elements and twelve animals. Every Fire Rat year is Yang, matching the Rat's own polarity.

Its traditional name is Bing-Zi: Bing is the yang Fire stem and Zi is the Rat's branch. Births just before each new year fall in the Wood Pig year (before January 24, 1936) and the Wood Pig year (before February 19, 1996), and births in the weeks after each Fire Rat year ends belong to the Fire Ox. The new year itself fell on a Friday in 1936 and Monday in 1996.

sections.heading: Growth edges and compatibility for the Fire Rat
paragraphs: Growth for the Fire Rat usually means learning to let the two currents cooperate instead of compete. Readings suggest a pause between feeling and responding, especially in arguments, where a Fire Rat's quick tongue can do damage that takes weeks to repair. Physical outlets such as running, dancing or demanding hobbies tend to burn off surplus heat. Because the combination enjoys novelty, it helps to choose a few long projects worth staying with even after the thrill has gone. When the Rat's natural caution is treated as a useful advisor rather than a brake to resent, the Fire Rat's boldness often lands well and earns lasting respect.

For relationships, the classical structures belong to the animal rather than the element, so the Fire Rat shares the Rat's San He trine with the Dragon and Monkey (the Water trine), its Liu He bond with the Ox, and its Liu Chong clash with the Horse. The element adds a second layer: another Fire sign shares this year element, while partners whose year element feeds Fire in the generating cycle are often described as supportive.

faq.question: What years are Fire Rat years?
faq.answer: Between 1924 and 2044: 1936 (from January 24, 1936) and 1996 (from February 19, 1996). Each lasts until the day before the next Lunar New Year.

faq.question: What is the Fire Rat's element relationship?
faq.answer: The year element is Fire and the Rat's fixed element is Water; in the five-element cycles water controls Fire. Readings use that relationship to describe how easily the two sides of the sign sit together.

faq.question: Which animals are most compatible with the Fire Rat?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Dragon and Monkey (San He) and the Ox (Liu He). The Horse is the Liu Chong clash. These pairings depend on the animal, whatever the element.

faq.question: What is the Fire Rat called in the Chinese calendar?
faq.answer: Bing-Zi. In almanacs and Four Pillars charts each year is named by its heavenly stem, here the Fire stem Bing, followed by its earthly branch, here Zi for the Rat, so the name pins down both halves of the combination at once.

faq.question: How is the Fire Rat different from other Rats?
faq.answer: All Rats share quick wits, resourcefulness and adaptability. The Fire year element changes the tone: fire is the element of summer and full daylight, and a Fire year is traditionally said to turn up the volume of whatever animal it meets.
